properties.name: The memoised walk is 60 ms through the shared daemon and a flat 5.8 s on plain stdio — same bytes, same binary, memo not taking effect on one of the two paths. Cause NOT established
properties.statement:
🛑 **A BOUND ON WHAT PR #479 ACTUALLY DELIVERED, FOUND HOURS AFTER MERGING IT, AND THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED.**

#479 memoised three derived scans per write generation and reported `propagate_from` at ~60 ms warm and `design_regions` at 12.5 s. Those numbers were taken **through the shared daemon**, and they are real — `design_regions` was re-run through it today, after the merge, and returned in seconds.

Driving the SAME binary over plain stdio against the SAME bytes tells a different story.

    four consecutive propagate_from calls, one process, no write between
    freshly imported copy   5506 / 5681 / 5488 / 5545 ms
    FILE-LEVEL copy of the
    live store              5858 / 5877 / 5712 / 5797 ms

**FLAT.** That is the exact signature used in #479 to identify work redone on every call — a memo that is hit drops after the first call and this does not drop at all. `design_regions` on that path ran past ten minutes and was stopped, which is consistent with ~5.8 s × 109 walks.

═══ WHAT THE MEASUREMENTS RULE OUT ═══

· **NOT the import, and NOT an uncompacted store.** The first run was a fresh `import_graph` copy, which made "bulk-loaded RocksDB with everything in L0" the obvious candidate. A **file-level `cp -r` of the live store — the identical bytes the fast daemon serves — behaves the same.** That kills it.
· **NOT the data.** Same 4,189 nodes either way.
· **NOT CPU contention.** A concurrent clippy finished partway through and the timings did not move.
· **NOT all reads.** On the same fresh copy a warm `get_node` is **3 ms, identical to the live store**, and a type scan is 54 ms against ~10 ms. Point reads are fine; only the walk collapses. So a blanket "that store is slow" does not fit either.

═══ WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS ═══

The difference that survives is the **server process**, not the data: the daemon holds one long-lived graph and the memo persists across calls; a plain stdio server appears not to benefit even across four calls inside ONE process, which is the part that does not yet make sense and is why no cause is written here.

⚠️ **NO CAUSE IS CLAIMED.** Four candidates were measured and killed; the remaining shape has not been isolated, and this project's own root-cause discipline says the first plausible explanation at the end of a long session is exactly what not to write down. The next step is the procedure, not a guess.

═══ WHY IT MATTERS TO A CONSUMER ═══

A session that attaches to the shared daemon gets the improvement. Anything driving reflow2 as a plain stdio child — a script, a CI step, a harness, possibly a first session before a daemon exists — may not. **#479's headline numbers are therefore true of one path and unverified on the other**, and that is a narrower claim than the PR made.

Found only because a coverage sweep wedged on `design_regions` and the 8-minute wall clock did not match the 12.5 s on the record — i.e. by a number looking odd, which is the trigger the root-cause skill names.
